failed_approaches: The first mutation attempt used a nonexistent contracts-generate recipe; just --list identified the confirm-gated contracts-gen command.
The first typed decode exposed serde rename_all spellings that omitted the required hyphen in AC-G-53/AC-G-07; explicit wire renames now match the normative profile IDs.
The preexisting two-root script copied only contracts/, so catalog-governed prose authorities were absent; it now copies both authorities and compares outputs solely through catalog edges.
serde_yaml_ng exposes no configurable pre-expansion alias cap, so the accepted subset rejects anchors and aliases before materialization.
The initial split-on-semicolon EBNF check was insufficient; it was replaced by a bounded tokenizer and recursive dialect parser.

Comparing a reordered catalog's full artifact-index bytes incorrectly ignored the required source_digest change; the reproduction oracle now separates unchanged-root byte reproducibility from reorder semantic invariance.
A direct prost-build dependency was retained initially but became redundant once tonic-prost-build compile_fds owned generation; it and the obsolete scanner exception were removed.
The loopback deadline probe can report either Cancelled or DeadlineExceeded at the local transport race boundary; the assertion now accepts exactly those two defined cancellation outcomes.
The tooling test import root was not visible under the adapter pytest rootdir until the recipe explicitly set PYTHONPATH=. for tooling/proto tests.
Importing FastMCP's concrete Tool class into the contract fingerprint module violated the framework-boundary structural rule; a protocol-facing structural Protocol now depends only on mcp.types.Tool.
The first fresh-target aggregate exposed seven all-target Clippy defects and was retained as correctness rather than timing evidence; the defects were corrected.
The second fresh-target aggregate exposed an overbroad root-wheel zero-state search that matched adapter-wheel-test; the rule now queries exact Just recipe keys.
A third full cold-target run was stopped because it measured unrelated Rust dependency rebuilds rather than the Python-only candidate boundary.

The first aggregate rerun correctly failed stable-graph-check because the exact contracts-tooling feature manifest did not yet include serde_path_to_error; the pin, feature edge, and graph assertion were added and the full aggregate reran green.
